notable_absence.finding: The page states the Search Service 'chooses reasonable defaults for the value of k1 and b' (the bm25 saturation and length-normalization parameters) but never states what those default numeric values actually are, nor points to a page that does - a reader who wants to know the literal default k1/b values has no path to that fact from this page.

cross_component_finding: This page documents running a Search query from SQL++ via the Query tab (tool:query-workbench) and the SEARCH() function, including explicit SQL++ code samples for conjunct (AND) vs disjunct (OR) combination of a regular Search query with a Vector Search knn clause - a genuine cross-component bridge between the search/ and n1ql/ doc trees, matching the same bridge already recorded on the Capella twin and the server/7.2 predecessor of this exact page.
cross_product_finding: Confirms the measured 0.92 similarity: this server/8.0 page and the Capella twin (cloud/search/run-searches.json) cover the same ground (UI/REST/SQL++/SDK entry points, tf-idf vs bm25 scoring gated behind 'Couchbase Server version 8.0') almost identically. One real divergence found: this server page gives substantially more mechanical detail on bm25 than the Capella twin's extraction captured - specifically the saturation parameter k1 ('Diminishing returns for a term that continues to frequently appear in documents') and the length-normalization parameter b ('adjustment to the resulting score, based on the total length of the current document field, divided by a normalized average length of the field across all documents'), plus a concrete tip about spam/clickbait scoring - none of which appear as concepts or relations in the Capella record, which only extracted the availableSince gate and the enum choice itself. The bm25-vs-tf-idf comparison and the SDK-language listing are otherwise structurally identical between the two pages.
